review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.issue: The ensemble and context were already fear-conditioned with the same footshock response. An increase can reflect strengthening, reconsolidation or generalization of that association; it does not identify a new association as claimed. Use neutral tagging or a distinguishable new outcome and outcome-specific assay.
The table reverses the stated Fos-tTA/TRE gate: doxycycline suppresses tTA-dependent labeling. The later off-Dox timeline conflicts with this table; resolve before execution.

errors.quote: Based on published contextual-fear effect sizes
errors.issue: No such published effect estimate is supplied or sourced. A retrieval effect size also does not establish power for the proposed acquisition interaction. Label the value as hypothetical and power the actual contrast from independent pilot data.

errors.quote: BLA c-Fos in G1 > G2/G3/G4 after Context-A test
errors.issue: The specified terminal collection is 90 minutes after Test 3, the optical probe in C, not the Context-A test. Those samples cannot identify A-retrieval activity; use separate terminal cohorts.

errors.quote: not* significantly elevated above other groups
errors.issue: A nonsignificant C difference does not rule out sensitization. Require the planned group-by-context contrast and a meaningful bound on generalization.

errors.quote: does not generate a plasticity-competent signal capable of forming new associations
errors.issue: A null under one stimulation and learning schedule cannot establish inability to support plasticity. Validate sensitivity and bound the conclusion to the tested parameters.
A direct DG-to-BLA projection is neither established by this packet nor validated by this design. Do not assume the proposed retrograde target exists or equate regional c-Fos with a direct route.

rationale: Includes controls, proposed settings and animal-level analysis, but its central same-context/same-fear increment cannot distinguish new association from modification of an old one. Contradictory gate instructions, unsupported published power premise, mismatched c-Fos sampling and overstrong null/generalization claims further reduce utility. Numerical detail alone does not repair identification.
reference_guardrails: Score scientific quality independently of historical matching. The open prompt permits defensible internal-outcome/second-order designs; these can earn high quality scores without matching the held-out neutral-context-as-CS experiment.

The draft target duplicates predicted_outcome text under mechanism. Interpret mechanism as a neutral context-associated ensemble acting as an internal conditioned cue; preserve the original key and disclose this clarification.

A previously fearful context gaining more freezing after additional same-valence conditioning does not uniquely identify a new association. Neutral labeling or a distinguishable new outcome is needed for that specific claim.
Doxycycline suppresses the proposed Fos-tTA/TRE label. Gate closure, expression maturation and neutral-context identity require separate validation; do not invent historical numerical settings.

Natural-context reactivation can occur without shock pairing; total tag counts do not establish context identity. Activity-marker overlap is supportive, not proof of storage, direct projections or subjective experience.

Matched unpaired exposure addresses contingency. Components-only controls do not fully replace it. Explicitly unpaired schedules can themselves support trace or safety learning, so retain other controls.

Primary no-light tests must precede potentially learning-altering optical probes or use independent cohorts. Slow terminal/endocrine measures after mixed events do not assign responses to a particular event.

Never remove artifact-positive control animals or high-freezing retrieval outcomes simply to satisfy a registered threshold. Retain assignment-based outcomes and explain technical/biological selection.
A null requires adequate assay validation and precision; source methods need not be copied. Broadly justified equivalent proposed methods earn credit.
Historical hits remain retrospective and do not certify novelty or an uncontaminated holdout. Earliest public disclosure and supplements are not fully audited.

review_sources.title: Ramirez et al. (2013), Creating a False Memory in the Hippocampus
review_sources.scope: Reviewer read main article and figure captions; excluded preceding unrelated article. Confirms neutral-context target and Dox gate direction. Supplementary methods, raw data and image integrity not audited. Reviewer-only source.
